summary:
The user selected baseline-relative review, one primary progress issue and complete bounded delegation. Dependents retain their own promise, Status and acceptance while linking to changing prerequisite detail. Review the known conditional sequence once, including collection and retirement, with separate original clocks, first-failure/Unknown stops and no automatic retry. Standing isolated verification and bounded read-only diagnostics acquire no additional permission gate. Keep one owner through publication and actual consumer adoption; preserve historical outcomes and evidence.

The optional evidence-manifest verify-delta route retains v1 compatibility. Caller-selected baseline/receipt SHA pins permit unchanged historical byte proofs to be inherited; changed payloads require bounded regular, non-link, stable reads. Source identities, original runs/limits, artifacts, reported acceptance and gaps remain visible. Inheritance proves neither current mutable-path bytes nor Git correspondence. Original failures and clock/limit types remain immutable; later observations do not replace them. Artifact verification leaves actual process/writer/cgroup/namespace/cleanup settlement and native acceptance Unknown. Manifests and receipts grant no authority or readiness and are not mandatory lifecycle records.

The issue observer uses fixed github.com comment GETs, one finite window, an original-request-bound successful cursor and a cooperative same-custody/request lock. It emits determining change (including edits), failure or deadline, starts no jobs and posts no messages. Partial reads preserve the last complete cursor; query and cleanup reserve precede reader launch. Cancellation/setup failures clean the owned reader before releasing its lock; direct-child reaping is not escaped-descendant settlement or hard containment. This source does not activate the separately qualified installed observe-operation route.

Actual consumer preflight found canonical Home4516/4517 history exceeded the four-page/400-comment bound. Optional RFC3339 --since now selects the existing request's fixed source/reply window, normalizes it to UTC and URL-encodes the same value on every page. Cursor and output disclose that window; a different baseline window refuses before lock acquisition or GET. The operation lock still binds repository, issues and original request, excluding since, so changing windows cannot create a second cooperating observer. Default None preserves unfiltered fail-closed behavior. Update-time filtering can include an older edited comment, but excludes history neither created nor updated since the boundary. The fixed window never advances during polling; bounded pages remain a sample, not an atomic or whole-history claim. Query, population, output and cleanup bounds remain unchanged.

Independent review originally held interrupted-reader custody, cross-original cursor adoption and Python bool/int/float equality rewriting original records. The same owner repaired them; the earlier20-control pass remains scoped to that source. After the consumer-window repair, the retained v1 fixture and24 causal controls passed in one bounded isolated run, including filtered pagination, edits, zero-lock/GET mismatch refusal, unchanged actual lock scope and overflow refusal. Both existing policy filters cover these files and the existing fixture invokes the controls; no extra workflow was created. Exact source review passed; protected delivery and first real Home adoption remain pending their own observations. Local reads/reuse are measured separately from reported intervention counts and source-ready-to-first-native latency. Missing inputs remain Unknown and token savings remain unmeasured.
title: Reuse accepted byte proofs and bound coordination attention
